questions.q: What is the relationship between OpenShift and Kubernetes?
o: OpenShift is a Kubernetes distribution with added security, builds, routes and Operators
OpenShift is an alternative orchestrator that replaces Kubernetes completely
Kubernetes is a plugin that runs inside an OpenShift cluster
They are the same product sold under two names by different vendors
questions.w: OpenShift contains standard Kubernetes, so Deployments, Services and ConfigMaps work unchanged. It adds platform features on top.

questions.q: An image that runs fine on Docker fails on OpenShift with permission errors. What is the most likely cause?
o: The default SCC runs it as a random non-root user, but the image expects root
OpenShift cannot pull images that were built on Docker
The router blocks all containers that expose port 8080
The image is too large for the integrated registry
questions.w: The restricted-v2 Security Context Constraint forces a random non-root UID (group 0). Fix the image rather than granting anyuid.

questions.q: In an OpenShift pod, files the application must write should be owned or writable by which group?
o: Group 0, because the random UID is always in the root group
The group named after the project
Group 1001, which every image must create at build time
No group, because OpenShift disables file permissions
questions.w: Use chgrp -R 0 and chmod -R g=u so the random user can write through its root group membership.

questions.q: What does an OpenShift Route do?
o: Publishes a Service on a hostname through the router, with TLS options and weights
Defines which node a pod is scheduled on, using labels and taints on the workers
Restricts which images may be pulled from the integrated registry by a project
Creates a Git webhook that starts a new build whenever a commit is pushed
questions.w: A Route is OpenShift's way to expose a Service externally. Ingress objects also work and are translated into Routes.

questions.q: Which Route TLS termination encrypts traffic on both the client leg and the leg to the pod while letting the router inspect requests?
o: Re-encrypt
Edge
Passthrough
None, routes cannot use TLS to the pod
questions.w: Edge ends TLS at the router, passthrough ends it at the pod without inspection, and re-encrypt does both legs with the router in the middle.

o: A build strategy that injects source into a builder image to create an image
A tool that converts a running container back into the source code it was built from
A network protocol for copying image layers between two registries in different clusters
A way of mounting a Git repository directly into a running pod as a writable volume
questions.w: S2I combines your code with a builder image (for example Java) and commits a runnable image. A BuildConfig describes it.

questions.q: What is an Operator in Kubernetes and OpenShift?
o: A controller that manages an application through a custom resource
A human administrator role that holds cluster-admin rights over every project
A command line plugin for oc that formats the output of get commands as tables
A type of node that runs only infrastructure pods such as the router and registry
questions.w: You declare desired state in a custom resource; the Operator reconciles the application to match. OLM installs and updates Operators.

questions.q: Which approach is recommended for new applications instead of the deprecated DeploymentConfig?
o: The standard Kubernetes Deployment
A bare Pod with a restart policy of Always
A StatefulSet for every stateless service
A Route with a replica count
questions.w: DeploymentConfig is deprecated; Deployment is portable and supports image triggers through annotations.
